title: Security of Approximate Neural Networks against Power Side-channel Attacks
problem: Security implications of approximate computing in Artificial Neural Networks; understanding vulnerability to power side-channel attacks as approximate computing techniques (overclocking, voltage scaling, bitwise approximation) are deployed for energy reduction.
motivation: Approximate computing reduces energy consumption in neural networks but may introduce security vulnerabilities; power side-channel attacks extract weights, and it is critical to understand whether approximation increases or decreases attack difficulty.
method: Evaluates power side-channel vulnerability of approximate ANN processing elements under three approximation scenarios: (1) overclocking, (2) voltage scaling, (3) circuit-level bitwise approximation. Performs weight extraction correlation power analysis (CPA) attacks; measures Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) degradation and Measurement-to-Disclosure (MTD) metric; analyzes trade-off via Security-Power-Delay (SPD) metric.
key_novelty: Comprehensive security analysis of approximate computing in ANNs against power side-channels, showing that approximation actually increases attack resistance (MTD increases 4x to >20x).
contributions: First security analysis of approximate ANNs against power side-channel CPA attacks
Demonstration that approximation increases SNR degradation and MTD (measurement difficulty)
Quantification: MTD of 48 (precise) increased to 200+ (bitwise 25% approx) or >1024 (voltage scaling)
Security-Power-Delay trade-off analysis showing voltage scaling as highest-performing technique

metrics.other: MTD improvement 4x-20x; SNR degradation analysis; Security-Power-Delay trade-off quantification

primary_theme: Power side-channel resistance of approximate neural networks
